new.title: Wander the three harbours of ancient Phaselis
new.desc: Phaselis was founded by Rhodian colonists around 690 BC and had three harbours, an aqueduct and a Roman agora in a pine forest by the sea. It later became a pirate haunt and a Byzantine port before decline.
new.tip: Come early or late to avoid tour buses; bring swimwear for the beaches inside the site.
new.q: Phaselis Antik Kenti, Tekirova, Kemer, Antalya

new.title: Stroll Kemer Marina at sunset
new.desc: Kemer Marina is a yacht harbour with space for around 320 boats, set below pine-covered mountains. The promenade is lined with cafés and shops, and boats leave from here for coastal cruises.
new.tip: Sunset gives the best light on the Beydağları peaks behind; evenings are busiest.

new.title: Swim at Moonlight Beach and Park in Kemer
new.desc: Moonlight Beach is a pebble beach just west of Kemer Marina, framed by hills and a landscaped park rather than hotel blocks. Entry to the beach is free.
new.tip: Swimming season runs late spring to October; go early for a sunbed.
new.q: Ayışığı Plajı ve Parkı, Yalı Caddesi No:16, Merkez Mahallesi, Kemer, Antalya

new.title: Walk the Göynük Canyon and cool off in its river
new.desc: Göynük Canyon is a narrow limestone gorge in the Beydağları foothills, about 13-15 km from Kemer, with walkways along a clear river. Kayaking is a popular activity here.
new.tip: Open daily roughly 09:00-17:30; bring water shoes and a swimsuit in summer.

new.title: Ride the Olympos Teleferik up Tahtalı to 2,365 m
new.desc: This Doppelmayr-Garaventa cable car climbs from 726 m to the summit of Tahtalı Dağı (Lycian Olympus) in about 10 minutes, in two 80-passenger cabins. The top gives views over the Gulf of Antalya and the Taurus range.
new.tip: Runs roughly 10:00-17:00 weather permitting; it is much colder at the top, so take a jacket.

new.title: Explore the ruins of ancient Olympos by the river
new.desc: Olympos was a Lycian city that later became a pirate stronghold and Roman port; its ruins of tombs, a theatre and a basilica lie in a wooded stream valley beside the beach. The Lycian Way passes straight through the site.
new.tip: A national park ticket covers entry; walk through to the beach at the end of the valley.
new.q: Olympos Antik Kenti, Olimpos, Kumluca, Antalya

new.title: See the eternal flames of Yanartaş (Chimaera) at night
new.desc: Natural methane vents burn on the slopes of Mount Olympos, a phenomenon recorded since antiquity and linked to the myth of the Chimaera monster. The flames are best seen after dark.
new.tip: Allow a 15-30 minute uphill walk from the car park; bring a torch and sturdy shoes.

new.title: Swim on Çıralı beach, a loggerhead turtle nesting site
new.desc: Çıralı is a long pebble beach in a quiet village of orange groves and pensions, set apart from the busier Olympos area. It lies within Beydağları Coastal National Park.
new.tip: Swim May to October; keep the shoreline dark at night in nesting season.

new.title: Drink at the Bull Bar of Kadir's Tree Houses in Olympos
new.desc: Kadir's is a long-running backpacker treehouse camp in the Olympos valley with restaurants, a rooftop terrace, a fire pit and the Bull Bar nightclub. It is the main social hub of the Olympos treehouse scene.
new.tip: Evening meals are included for guests but non-guests can drink at the bars; expect a young crowd in summer.
new.q: Kadir's Tree Houses, Olimpos, Kumluca, Antalya

new.title: Eat gözleme and mantı at Yörük Restaurant in Çıralı
new.desc: A restaurant just after the bridge into Çıralı, praised by Lonely Planet for Turkish food cooked in an open kitchen: gözleme, pide and mantı.
new.tip: Order the gözleme straight from the griddle; a good lunch before the Chimaera walk.

new.title: Have gözleme from the organic garden at Çıralı Gözleme
new.desc: A family-run restaurant in Çıralı where the vegetables come from the owners' own organic garden and greenhouse, and gözleme is made to order.
new.tip: Cheap and quick; ask for the seasonal vegetable filling.

new.title: Try home-style Turkish dishes at Ceylan in Çıralı
new.desc: Ceylan Restaurant & Bar is a sit-down place in Çıralı that reviewers describe as one of few spots serving authentic Turkish home cooking rather than tourist menus.
new.tip: Ask for the daily home-cooked dishes; reservations are not usually needed.

new.title: Catch your own trout at Botanik Restaurant in Ulupınar
new.desc: Ulupınar, near the Chimaera, is known for stream-side trout restaurants, and Botanik lets guests net a trout from the pool and have it fried to order.
new.tip: Pair it with a Chimaera visit; avoid the mountain road after dark if you are not driving.

new.title: Take a boat from Adrasan to Suluada island
new.desc: Adrasan is a sheltered bay below the Musa mountains; boats run from its harbour to Suluada island, 2 km offshore near Cape Gelidonya, for swimming in clear water.
new.tip: Boats run roughly April to October; book at the harbour in the morning.

new.title: Hike the Lycian Way from Adrasan to Olympos
new.desc: This stage of the Lycian Way runs from Adrasan over the Musa mountains and down through the ruins of Olympos to Çıralı, about 15.5 km by Trekopedia's figures.
new.tip: Start early; carry plenty of water and avoid midsummer midday heat.

new.title: Hike the Lycian Way from Karaöz to Gelidonya
new.desc: The Karaöz to Adrasan leg is a long, rugged coastal stage that passes the Gelidonya lighthouse, standing on the southernmost point of ancient Lycia.
new.tip: A demanding day; start early, carry water and check the trail with locals.

new.title: Reach the Cape Gelidonya lighthouse
new.desc: Cape Gelidonya is the southernmost headland of ancient Lycia, topped by a lighthouse. A Bronze Age shipwreck found offshore was excavated here in 1960, one of the first underwater archaeological digs.
new.tip: Reached by the Lycian Way or boat; road access is rough, so go on foot or with a local guide.

new.title: Spend a day at Mavikent beach in Kumluca
new.desc: Kumluca is Turkey's major greenhouse district, producing tomatoes, peppers and citrus along the coast below the Beydağları; Mavikent beach has a calmer, local feel.
new.tip: Best in spring; a car helps.

new.title: Climb the terraces of Arykanda
new.desc: Arykanda is a Lycian hill city on terraces in the Beydağları with a theatre, stadium, baths and an agora, founded by the 4th century BC. It is considered among the best-preserved sites in Lycia.
new.tip: About 30 km inland from the Finike D400 junction; go in the morning in summer.
new.q: Arykanda Antik Kenti, Arif, Finike, Antalya

new.title: See the rock tombs and mausoleum of Limyra
new.desc: Limyra was a Lycian capital with more than 400 rock tombs, many inscribed in the Lycian language, and the mausoleum of king Perikle. Excavations began in 1970.
new.tip: Quiet and little visited; a taxi from Finike is easiest.
new.q: Limyra Antik Kenti, Turunçova, Finike, Antalya

new.title: Eat fish soup and fried squid at Neşeli Balık in Finike
new.desc: Regarded as Finike's best fish restaurant, in a historic stone building in the back streets, known for fish soup, fried squid and balık ekmek.
new.tip: Try the fish soup first; lunch is quieter than dinner.
new.q: Neşeli Balık, Finike Merkez, Finike, Antalya

new.title: Eat fresh fish at Neşeli Balık on Finike's Atatürk Caddesi
new.desc: Neşeli Balık is a well-reviewed seafood restaurant on Atatürk Caddesi, Finike's main eating street running north from the marina. Its menu covers fish and seafood alongside salads and grills.
new.tip: Book ahead for dinner in summer and check hours, which run roughly from morning to about 22:30.
new.q: Neşeli Balık, Atatürk Caddesi No:49, Finike, Antalya

new.title: Taste olive-oil-and-salt grills at Altın Sofra in Finike
new.desc: Altın Sofra is a Finike restaurant where the chef grills meat and chicken using only olive oil and salt.
new.tip: Order the grills; ask about Finike oranges for dessert in season.
new.q: Altın Sofra, Finike Merkez, Finike, Antalya

new.title: Visit the Church of St Nicholas in Demre
new.desc: The church of the 4th-century bishop of Myra, the original Santa Claus, has Byzantine frescoes and mosaics; the main structure dates mostly from the 5th century or later. His relics were taken to Bari in 1087.
new.tip: A museum ticket applies; go early to avoid tour groups.

new.title: See the Lycian rock tombs and theatre of Myra
new.desc: Myra has two necropolises of temple-fronted tombs carved into cliff faces, with over 100 rock tombs, plus a large Roman theatre at their foot.
new.tip: Visit the river necropolis first, then the theatre; go in the morning light.

new.title: Explore the Roman harbour granary of Andriake
new.desc: Andriake was Myra's port until silt blocked its entrance. The site has a granary built under Hadrian, now a museum, and port remains by a river mouth.
new.tip: Combine with a seafood lunch at Çayağzı.
new.q: Andriake Antik Limanı, Çayağzı, Demre, Antalya

new.title: Eat grilled sea bass and blue crab at Memedim Balık in Demre
new.desc: A basic, authentic eatery by the lagoon in Demre known for grilled fish and the local blue crab.
new.tip: Pick the grilled sea bass; the blue crab has little meat.
new.q: Memedim Balık Restoran, Çayağzı, Demre, Antalya

new.title: Take a boat trip to Kekova's sunken city from Üçağız
new.desc: Day boats leave Üçağız harbour for the sunken Lycian ruins around Kekova island, with a swim stop at Aquarium Bay and a visit to Kaleköy. Swimming among the ruins is prohibited.
new.tip: Boats leave around 10:30; book the day before; Tersane Bay is the swimming spot.

new.title: Climb to Simena castle at Kaleköy
new.desc: Kaleköy, ancient Simena, is the only Mediterranean village in Turkey without road access; a small castle and Lycian sarcophagi stand above the bay.
new.tip: Arrive by boat from Üçağız and climb to the castle for the view over the sunken ruins.

new.title: See the Lycian King's Tomb at the top of Uzun Çarşı in Kaş
new.desc: This 4th-century BC Lycian sarcophagus on a high base, also called the Lion Tomb, stands at the top of Uzun Çarşı, a steep cobbled lane of old Greek houses.
new.tip: Walk up Uzun Çarşı and visit at dusk.
new.q: Kral Mezarı (Aslanlı Lahit), Uzun Çarşı Sokak, Kaş, Antalya

new.title: Watch the sunset from the Antiphellos theatre in Kaş
new.desc: This small Hellenistic theatre dates from the 1st century BC, restored in 2008, with seating for about 4,000 and sea views from the top rows.
new.tip: About 500 m west of the main square; free to enter.

new.title: Take the ferry from Kaş to Greek Meis (Kastellorizo)
new.desc: Daily ferries cross to the Greek island of Meis in about 20-25 minutes in summer, a day trip with passport control.
new.tip: Bring your passport and book the day before so the operator can process immigration paperwork.

new.title: Dive the reefs and wrecks around Kaş
new.desc: Kaş is Turkey's best-known diving base, with a cluster of dive centres and underwater sites around the nearby islands.
new.tip: Choose a licensed centre; dives run in the warm months.

new.title: Start the day with breakfast and mezes at Bi Lokma in Kaş
new.desc: A family-run all-day restaurant in central Kaş, open 08:30 to midnight, praised for breakfast, mezes and manti.
new.tip: They rarely take reservations, so arrive early at weekends.
new.q: Bi'Lokma, Uğur Mumcu Caddesi 21, Kaş, Antalya

new.title: Try saç kavurma at Smiley's in Kaş
new.desc: A seafood restaurant in Kaş, where reviewers single out the saç kavurma. Prices are mid to high.
new.tip: Compare prices before ordering fish by weight.
new.q: Smiley's Restaurant, Kaş Merkez, Kaş, Antalya

new.title: Have dessert and traditional food at Sardunya in Kaş
new.desc: Sardunya is a family-run traditional Turkish restaurant and café in Kaş, noted for desserts and cosy atmosphere.
new.tip: Good for an after-dinner dessert and tea.
new.q: Sardunya Restaurant, Kaş Merkez, Kaş, Antalya

new.title: Swim at Büyük Çakıl Beach in Kaş
new.desc: A pebble beach on the east side of Kaş, reached on foot from the old town, with sea views toward Meis.
new.tip: Take shoes for the pebbles; summer weekends are busy.

new.title: Swim at Kaputaş beach below the cliff road
new.desc: Kaputaş is a small sandy beach in a narrow gorge reached by steps from the Kaş-Kalkan road, 15-21 km from Kaş.
new.tip: Arrive early; the steps are steep and it is crowded in July and August.
new.q: Kaputaş Plajı, Kaş-Kalkan Yolu, Kaş, Antalya

new.title: Wander Kalkan's old town and harbour
new.desc: Kalkan's old Greek houses and narrow lanes climb above a small harbour, with rooftop restaurants and sea views.
new.tip: Go at sunset and walk down to the harbour for dinner.
new.q: Kalkan Eski Şehir, Kalkan, Kaş, Antalya

new.title: Dine at Trio on Kalkan harbour
new.desc: Trio is a harbour restaurant serving Turkish, Mediterranean and international dishes, rated around 4.1 on Google.
new.tip: Book a harbour-view table for sunset.
new.q: Trio Restaurant, Kalkan Limanı, Kalkan, Kaş, Antalya

new.title: Dine on meze at Kalamaki in Kalkan's old town
new.desc: Kalamaki is a casually stylish restaurant-bar in Kalkan's old town, serving meze, fusion and traditional Turkish dishes. Fodor's lists it among the area's recommended places.
new.tip: Come at sunset for a table with a view and reserve in high season.

new.title: Eat tender kebabs at Mabeyn in Kalkan
new.desc: Mabeyn is a Kalkan restaurant praised by reviewers for smoky, tender kebabs.
new.tip: Order the mixed grill.

new.title: Walk Patara's ancient city and theatre
new.desc: Patara was the main port of Lycia, with a restored bouleuterion, a large theatre, Roman baths and the oldest known lighthouse.
new.tip: Wear a hat; there is little shade.
new.q: Patara Antik Kenti, Gelemiş, Kaş, Antalya

new.title: Walk the long dunes of Patara beach
new.desc: Patara beach is a 12 km stretch of sand, among the longest in Turkey, and a loggerhead turtle nesting site.
new.tip: Swim May to October; closed after dark in nesting season.

new.title: See the Lycian tombs and theatre of Xanthos
new.desc: Xanthos was the capital of ancient Lycia; UNESCO listed the site with Letoon. Some relics were removed to the British Museum in the 19th century.
new.tip: Pair with Letoon and Saklıkent on one day.
new.q: Xanthos Antik Kenti, Kınık, Seydikemer, Muğla

new.title: Visit the Letoon sanctuary near Xanthos
new.desc: Letoon was the federal sanctuary of Lycia, with foundations of three temples to Leto, Apollo and Artemis. UNESCO World Heritage.
new.tip: Often flooded in spring; visit in summer.
new.q: Letoon Antik Kenti, Kumluova, Seydikemer, Muğla

new.title: Wade through Saklıkent Gorge
new.desc: Saklıkent is an 18 km gorge up to 300 m deep with an icy river; visitors walk the floor, with rafting and canyoning available.
new.tip: Wear water shoes and bring a change of clothes.

new.title: Seek out Yeşil Göl and Uçarsu waterfall above Gömbe
new.desc: Yeşil Göl (Green Lake) and Uçarsu Waterfall lie on Akdağ above Gömbe, a highland of cedars and apple orchards at about 1,200 m.
new.tip: Highland roads; best from late spring to autumn.
new.q: Uçarsu Şelalesi ve Yeşil Göl, Gömbe, Kaş, Antalya

new.title: Wander Elmalı, Turkey's apple town
new.desc: Elmalı produces about 12 percent of Turkey's apples and is known for leblebi roasted chickpeas, with a cedar research forest nearby.
new.tip: Visit in autumn for the apple harvest.

new.title: Walk the Çukurbağ peninsula at sunset
new.desc: The wooded Çukurbağ peninsula west of Kaş has coastal paths, small coves and sunset views over Meis.
new.tip: Walk from the Antiphellos theatre side; take water.
